chapter_title: Concerning the Nourishment of the Person, for ther

fills.notes: Opening clause needs a subject for “exists … daily to the body.” In the substrate register, the constant influx/operation of a cosmic “power” (not a personal savior) fits the correspondential logic of a daily action upon the body.
Connects the daily operation “to the body of the person” with the ensuing anatomical/cosmic enumeration of “seals” and “rulers.”
Parallelism: “there are two hundred and fifty thousand seals in it … there are another two hundred and fifty thousand rulers …” requires a simple connective at each step.
After listing the two sets, the text shifts to their action (“they are cleansed…”). A transition like “of it; and when” matches the move from static constitution to process.

Cleansed powers entering a receptacle corresponds to purified influxes being received/collected in a higher vessel. “Storehouse/treasury” is substrate-cosmological (impersonal), avoiding later ecclesial framing.

The triad “voice, word, and …” demands a third term that is not explicitly Christian-personal but denotes ordered degrees/operations. “Measures” fits correspondentially (distinct degrees) and can be named as a set of three.

“quiet with the silence” needs a governing verb phrase describing the heart’s state-change. Stillness/rest is the correspondential effect of ordered influx (voice/word/measures) when the interior is set in equilibrium.

The phrase modifies “rulers that belong to the Darkness.” The oldest layer tends to classify by function (archontic/ruling) rather than moral exhortation; “great archontic rulers” matches the cosmological taxonomy.

“swept out outside in wandering and in transmigration …” is followed naturally by a spatial-cosmological qualifier: wandering occurs “in the circuits” (revolutions/rounds), aligning with transmigratory motion.
Syntax requires a verb governing “this transmigration.” “Pass through” is the minimal, structurally correct reading and preserves the impersonal, process-based register.

assessment: Only a small amount of contiguous wording survives around each gap, so most restorations are constrained mainly by parallelism (enumerations, triads), required syntax, and the substrate’s impersonal cosmological register. The most secure is ¶2 #3 (“shall pass through”), which is syntactically forced. The triadic slot after “voice” and “word” is structurally constrained but lexically uncertain; other connectives and transition phrases are plausible but remain tentative.
